1	# Project Landing Page - notes
2	
3	A project's own page (`/f/<id>`), a redesign of `server/views/_folder.eta` (with
4	`_branch.eta`), whose model is built in `server/main.js` (`view()` in the
5	`/f/:id` handler). Home (prelude/landing-page) gathers what needs the person
6	across projects and links here; this page holds the project's whole picture.
7	
8	Pages: `/f/:project` (Project), `/f/:project/designs/new` (New design, modal),
9	`/f/:project/branches/:branch/publish` (Push a branch, modal). Fragments:
10	`/f/:project/work`, `/f/:project/app`. States: typical (spark-lending), new
11	project, app being built, update clashed (with the app on the shell's branch
12	and a failed push), long names (an existing app to connect, no remote),
13	large project (a hundred features).
14	
15	## Decisions (the person asked for all eleven, 2026-10-18)
16	
17	1. **On the design system**, not ds/v1 + `prelude.css`, like Home.
18	2. **Work beside setup**: a `.split` in a `.center.wide`. Main: Needs you, In
19	   progress, Designs. Side: The app, What the agent can read. Added
20	   `.center.wide` / `--measure-wide` to the design system (46rem can't hold a
21	   split).
22	3. **New design is a modal**, opened by the header's "New design…", the page's
23	   one primary action. A refused title comes back into the fields alone
24	   (`_new-design-fields`); made, the modal closes and the page refreshes (the
25	   real app opens the new design's page).
26	4. **One primary per view**: Merge, Push, Start the app build are plain buttons.
27	5. **A branch's state as pills**: check, building / build stopped, behind main,
28	   pull request open, nothing done yet. Stories get a state pill (Built, To
29	   build, Building) and "A change". "Also changes" is a disclosure with the
30	   full list.
31	6. **Designs show progress**: pages and how many approved or built, and when
32	   they last changed. Grouped by area, those with none (system, shell) first.
33	   A plain "Ready to build" pill when

text:
1	# The design system and app shell say what they hold
2	
3	For anyone looking down a project's designs to see how far each has got. Today the design system and the app shell are counted by their pages, as a feature is. The design system has no pages: its screens are a gallery of components. The shell's gallery is left out on purpose. So both say "nothing designed yet", or count gallery screens as pages, even when they're finished and in use. Once this is built, each one describes itself by what it actually holds. A person can then tell at a glance that they're done and don't need any more work.
4	
5	## What changes
6	
7	- Under Designs, the design system's line counts its components, e.g. "tokens and 24 components", rather than pages.
8	- The app shell's line counts its layouts, and any pages of its own beside them, e.g. "2 layouts" or "3 layouts and 1 page".
9	- Once the project's app exists, the shell's line also says how much of that is built: "all built", "1 built" or "none built yet". Before the app exists, it gives only the count.
10	- A design system with no components yet, or a shell with no layouts or pages, still says "nothing designed yet".
11	- Feature designs are counted by their pages, as they are today.
12	
13	## Acceptance criteria
14	
15	- In a project whose design system has components, its row under Designs reads "tokens and N components" (with "1 component" when there is only one), followed by when it last changed.
16	- A design system with no components reads "nothing designed yet".
17	- The app shell's row reads "N layouts". When the shell has pages of its own, the row reads "N layouts and M pages", with "layout" and "page" in the singular for one.
18	- When the project's app exists, the shell's row ends with "all built" when every layout and page is built. When only some are built, it ends with how many are built. When none is built, it ends with "none built yet".
19	- When the project's app doesn't exist yet, the shell's row gives the count

1	// Design hosts for other stacks (plan: step 6c).
2	//
3	// A repository whose app renders its own views - another stack, or (step 8)
4	// the app a first build creates, which is its own design host - names it in a
5	// committed prelude/prelude.json:
6	//
7	//   { "host": { "start": "dotnet run --project App --urls http://localhost:5199",
8	//               "url": "http://localhost:5199", "views": ".cshtml",
9	//               "guide": "prelude/HOST.md" } }
10	//
11	// The host only renders: Prelude keeps routes, data, forms, overlays and the
12	// rest, and asks it, over HTTP, to render a view with a model inside a layout
13	// (the same job the sandboxed Eta renderer does). The contract:
14	//
15	//   GET  /__prelude/health   200 once ready
16	//   POST /__prelude/render   { root, page: { views, template, data },
17	//                              layout: { views, template, data } | { default: true, data } | null,
18	//                              regions: { <name>: { views, template, data, location } },
19	//                              query }
20	//                            -> 200 text/html, or 500 with the engine's error as text.
21	//                               A 200 may say x-prelude-ahead: <members>: state members
22	//                               a typed view's model doesn't have yet (the design is
23	//                               ahead of the app). Reported, never failed (step 7).
24	//   GET  <anything else>     the app's own static assets, at their real paths
25	//
26	// Paths in a render are relative to the repository (`root`), with forward
27	// slashes; templates have no extension (the host's is `views`). A layout of
28	// { default: true } is the host's own minimal layout. Each view sees the query
29	// as $query, and a refused form's messages as $errors in its data.
30	//
Now the view port, routes, and notes.

I've built the change: the design system and the app shell now say what they hold under Designs. I couldn't run anything myself, so Prelude's render after this turn is the first real check.

**What changed**
- **`server/views/projects/_designs.eta`**: I copied the redesigned view over the app's, element for element. The design system's line reads "tokens and N components". The shell's reads "N layouts" or "N layouts and M pages", and once the app exists it adds "all built", "N built" or "none built yet". Either one with nothing in it reads "nothing designed yet". Feature lines read as before.
- **`server/views/projects/page.eta`**: the design's version is identical to the app's, so I left it alone.
- **`server/project.js`**: `progressOf()` now counts the design system's components (its `system/components/*.html` files). For the shell it adds `layouts` and `layoutsBuilt`, worked out with `unbuiltLayouts`. `layoutsBuilt` stays 0 until the app exists. The model's `Design` type gains `components`, `layouts` and `layoutsBuilt`, all optional, so every state still fits.
- **`routes.json`**: both routes now point at `@app/server/views/projects/…`, and their `from` is removed.
- **`NOTES.md`**: added a short "Built" note. The story and the design agree, so there's nothing to report there. `RULES.md` had no proposed rules, so it's unchanged.

**One decision for you to check:** I made each design's `stage` (which drives the Ready to build / Still designing filter) follow what the states show. Without that, a finished design system would have shown up under "Still designing". Now:
- a design system with components is `built` once the app exists and `approved` before it;
- a design system with no components is `designing`;
- a shell is `built` when all its layouts and own pages are built.

**Before approving the screens:** the approved snapshots predate this change. They still show the system and shell as "3 pages, all built", so the comparison will flag differences on every Designs list. That's expected. Check the new wording against the story's "Looks right in" list:
- **Typical:** "tokens and 24 components" and "2 layouts, all built"
- **Large project:** "tokens and 31 components" and "3 layouts and 1 page, all built"
- **App being built and Update clashed:** "tokens and 18 components"
- **Long names:** "nothing designed yet"
- **New project:** the first-run page, unchanged

Then take the snapshots again for those states.

The Work page (`/f/:project/work`) is also listed as looking different in typical, update-clashed and large-project. Nothing in this change touches its view or its data, so if it still differs after the render, those differences come from somewhere else.
Committed to prelude/project-landing-page (d388687).
